about.title: Ojai Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Ojai's small-town charm brings foot traffic to its historic downtown, arcade shops, and outdoor spaces near Libbey Park and the surrounding trails — but uneven pavement, loose mats, poor lighting, or spills can turn a pleasant walk into a serious injury. California law requires an injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting conditions matters so much here: photos of a cracked walkway on Ojai Avenue, a puddle near a Cuyama Road storefront entrance, or missing signage can make the difference in a claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in the network who can evaluate what happened, gather evidence before it disappears, and explain your options. There's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Ojai Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Key Legal Question
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help identify evidence — like prior complaints or maintenance logs — that supports this notice requirement.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Ojai businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. An attorney connected through LawProactive can move quickly to send preservation letters before that evidence is lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly accounts for shared responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Ojai?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability claim. If the property involved is owned by a public entity — such as a city sidewalk or county building — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Because of this, it's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible after the fall.

items.question: What if the fall happened at a small local shop in downtown Ojai?
items.answer: Ojai's downtown includes many small, independently owned businesses, and the same premises liability principles apply regardless of business size. What matters is whether the owner or occupier knew or should have known about the hazardous condition. An attorney can help investigate the specific circumstances, including whether the business had any record of prior complaints about the area.

items.question: Do I need to prove the property owner was careless?
items.answer: You need to show the owner had notice of the dangerous condition and failed to address it within a reasonable time. This can include evidence that the hazard existed long enough that a reasonably careful owner should have discovered it. Photos, witness accounts, and maintenance records often help establish this.
